title: Lienholder Refund Release Amount and Late-Release Interest
content:
## Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda: amount of a refund released to the lienholder

**Clause.** The lienholder release pays the refund due, which is the amount of the refund calculation entry on the waiver's ledger. The effective date of the cancellation is the waiver's closing date, or the release date where the waiver carries none. The late window of a lienholder release starts on the effective date of the cancellation. Where the release is made more than the refund payment period of the waiver's tier (in calendar days) after the late window starts, late-release interest is added on the refund due at 0.05 a year (5 percent) for each calendar day past that refund payment period after the window start, counted on a 365-day year and rounded half up to the cent. The lienholder release amount is the refund due plus the late-release interest, rounded half up to the cent. A lienholder release is not made for a refund due of 0.00, and it is made only on a waiver with no loan payoff date on file; on any other waiver the lienholder release amount is 0.00.

### Quantities

| Quantity | Read from |
|---|---|
| Refund due | The refund calculation entry on the waiver's ledger |
| Effective date of the cancellation | The waiver's closing date; the release date where none is recorded |
| Late days | Calendar days from the late-window start to the release date, less the refund payment period, never below zero |
| Late-release interest | Refund due times 0.05 times late days, divided by 365, rounded half up to the cent |
| Release amount | Refund due plus late-release interest, rounded half up to the cent |

The refund payment period is the figure the waiver's tier shows in the cancellation and refund terms of the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda.

### Points of judgement

- A release made on or before the last day of the refund payment period after the window start carries no late-release interest: the late days are zero.
- One day past that period counts as one late day.
- The interest is rounded to the cent on its own, then added to the refund due.

### Illustration (hypothetical figures)

A waiver's refund calculation entry shows 412.37; its closing date is Day 0, and its tier's refund payment period is 30 days. The release is made on Day 47.

1. Late days: 47 less 30, which is 17.
2. Late-release interest: 412.37 times 0.05 times 17, divided by 365, is 0.9603…, rounded half up to 0.96.
3. Release amount: 412.37 plus 0.96, which is 413.33.

Had the release been made on Day 30, the late days would be zero and the release amount would be 412.37.
